_README: Copy this to vault/settings/search.json, then REPLACE EVERY PLACEHOLDER. vault/ is never committed.
The angle-bracket values below are placeholders, not defaults. Left as they are,
the location filter matches nothing and the radar returns nothing.
Nothing in this file should describe a real person until you fill it in yourself.
queries: <a third — 10 to 40 queries is a sensible range>

_comment: Plain substrings, matched case-insensitively against the posting's location.
'ok' alone wins nothing; 'bad' and 'edge' both exclude. Add 'remote' to ok if
you want remote roles — but note that most boards scope remote to one country.
edge: <somewhere you would consider only for the right role>

adzuna._comment: Free key from https://developer.adzuna.com/ . country is an ISO-2 code. Coverage varies by country — check yours is supported before relying on it.

_watch_comment: Name employers here and the endpoint is looked up in ats_registry.json -- no need to know whether
they use Greenhouse, Workday or Oracle. Anything that cannot be resolved is reported at the
start of every run rather than quietly skipped. Run `python3 tools/radar/registry.py NAME` to
test a name, and `python3 tools/registry_check.py` to confirm the endpoints still answer.
🔴 This shipped naming two REAL employers until 2026-08-26 -- taken from one user's own
watch list. A template that says REPLACE EVERY PLACEHOLDER and then quietly carries
somebody's actual answers teaches the reader that some of it is already right.
_postings_comment: Where to archive the description of every shortlisted role. Default: ../../wiki/postings.
A posting is the evidence behind a score, a requirement tally and an interview story, and it is
the one input guaranteed to be deleted -- usually right when it becomes useful. Never overwritten:
an archived posting records what was actually read at the time.
watch: <an employer you want watched by name>

greenhouse._comment: Board tokens of employers you want watched directly. Find one in their careers URL: boards.greenhouse.io/<token>

_comment: Employers whose careers site runs on Workday — a large share of big ones do,
even where the site looks bespoke. No key needed.
host, tenant and site are THREE SEPARATE VALUES and you cannot derive one from
another: there are two hosting styles and an adapter that assumes either one
misses the other silently.
per-tenant:  <tenant>.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com   shared: wd1.myworkdaysite.com
The shard number varies (wd1/wd3/wd5). A 422 means the wrong shard, not a bad
request — the adapter says so when it sees one.
Read all three values off the employer's careers URL, which looks like:
https://<host>/en-US/<site>/job/...
'names' is optional and only prettifies the tenant slug in the shortlist.
Employers on Oracle Cloud Recruiting. No key needed, and unlike Workday it needs
only TWO values — both are in the careers URL, which looks like:
https://<host>/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/<site>/jobs
Take host and site verbatim. Do not derive the host: tenants appear both with a
region (<pod>.fa.us2.oraclecloud.com) and without (<pod>.fa.oraclecloud.com).
'names' is optional and only prettifies the site slug in the shortlist.

linkedin._comment: OFF by default. Undocumented endpoint, against LinkedIn's terms of service. Read adapters/linkedin.py and decide for yourself.

_comment: Google runs its own careers site: no third-party ATS, and no JSON API (the old
careers.google.com/api/v3 endpoint answers 404). The results page is SERVER-RENDERED,
so the adapter reads the HTML directly. Leave 'locations' empty to disable this source.
'locations' are Google's own location strings, exactly as they appear in the ?location=
parameter of the careers URL. Their site writes 'Dublin Ireland', not 'Dublin, Ireland' --
open the careers page, filter to your city, and copy the value out of the address bar.
🔴 GOOGLE PUBLISHES NO POSTING DATE anywhere on a job card. Worse than Workday's
'30+ days', which at least gives you a floor. Rows carry an empty date and may be any
age, so never report a Google role as new.
pages is a budget of 20 roles each. The adapter stops early on a short page or a repeat,
so a generous number costs nothing when the board is smaller than the budget.
